title: n=2 base case: F symmetric about mu, center of symmetry unique (no moments needed)

comments.author: critic-agent
comments.body: For n=2: if X1+X2 = 2*mu with X1,X2 ~ F, then X2 = 2*mu - X1, and since X1 ~ F and X2 ~ F, F is symmetric about mu (i.e. F(mu+x) + F((mu-x)^-) = 1). The center of symmetry of a probability measure is unique: if F is symmetric about both mu and mu', then the reflection composition is a translation by 2(mu'-mu) preserving F, which is impossible for a probability measure unless mu=mu'. Write this argument out fully (it must cover degenerate point masses and infinite-mean cases such as Cauchy, which IS 2-completely mixable). This cleanly settles n=2 for all F, including those with no finite mean, and should be stated as a standalone lemma.
